summary: Rate-limit tuning for scheduled model warmups and bulk writes causing intermittent 429s
description:
Issue summary:
Customer runs nightly scheduled model warmup jobs + hourly bulk embedding writes to their dedicated pool. Over the last 48 hours they started seeing intermittent 429s during the overlap window where warmups and large uploads run concurrently.

Impact:
- ~15% of warmup requests receive 429s, resulting in incomplete warmup and elevated latency for first user requests.
- A portion of bulk embeddings fail and are retried from the customer side, increasing downstream backlogs and cost.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (customer-managed reservation) in prod:us-east-1, pool id dpool-04f2
- Warmup jobs: scheduled cron job, hits /v1/serving/generate with short sequences (max_tokens=16) and concurrency 20
- Bulk writes: parallel uploader with 40 workers doing batching (batch_size=64) against embeddings endpoint /v1/embeddings

Steps to reproduce (customer supplied):
1) Trigger warmup job immediately after scheduled bulk run start.
2) Observe 429s in warmup job logs for ~10-20 minutes.
3) If bulk finishes first, warmups usually succeed.

Observed behavior:
- 429s return "rate_limit_exceeded" and headers show X-RateLimit-Policy: "tenant-token-window-v2"
- Throttling appears more common when bulk workers use short lived collateral API keys (rotated per worker) and uploader spikes concurrency.

Expected behavior:
- Warmups (short low-cost traces) should be able to proceed even during bulk embedding windows, or at a minimum there should be clear documentation and a recommended configuration to avoid this impact.

Customer ask:
- Guidance on rate-limit settings and recommended separation of traffic classes for warmup vs bulk uploads.
- If we can increase the short-window per-key concurrency for warmup endpoints or suggest a config that isolates warmup calls from bulk writes in their dedicated pool.

investigation_notes: Log correlation shows tenant token-window exhaustion: many distinct API keys increment per-key counters but tenant-level window is aggregated, causing earlier-than-expected throttles.

Rate limiter behavior: per-key short-window and tenant aggregated window both enforced. High cardinality of keys with concurrent small requests magnifies token consumption due to per-request overhead tracking.
Serving runtime metrics indicate warmup requests are low-cost but are counted against the same token budget as embeddings which are heavier and issued in larger batches.
Confirmed that the dedicated pool uses default short-window sizing. No custom per-route soft-allowances currently configured for this customer.

Risk analysis: increasing tenant-wide window may affect isolation guarantees between customers on shared control plane components; per-route soft-allowance is lower risk for dedicated pool since it can be scoped to the pool id.
resolution_notes: Short-term workaround provided: 1) recommend uploader reuse a smaller pool of long-lived keys (reduces cardinality), 2) stagger warmup start by 10 minutes after bulk start, 3) temporarily lower uploader concurrency to 24. Customer reports partial improvement.

Medium-term action: engineering to add per-route soft-allowance config for dedicated pools to allow low-cost warmup endpoints a protected token band during scheduled windows. PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/rate-limiter/pull/142 created and under review.

Follow-up: SRE to run a canary for the soft-allowance on dpool-04f2 during a maintenance window next week (INT-4021). If canary is green, we will offer the configuration as an opt-in for dedicated customers.

Documentation: Update runbook and customer guidance page with recommended patterns: reuse keys for high-cardinality uploaders, tag low-cost warmup routes, schedule warmups outside high-throughput windows. Confluence page link updated.
Status: awaiting engineering canary and customer confirmation after tonight's scheduled warmup. Support will remain point of contact until resolved.
